stem: A recipient calls reporting new drainage from the surgical wound. According to urgent-contact education, how should the coordinator classify this finding?

options.text: An urgent matter requiring prompt transplant team contact
A non-urgent matter appropriate for the next routine refill call
An expected finding that never requires notification
A reason to stop all immunosuppression without medical guidance

explanation.rationale_correct: New drainage from the wound is listed among urgent matters requiring prompt transplant team contact, alongside infection symptoms, chest pain, and bleeding.

rationale_incorrect.B: New wound drainage is explicitly urgent rather than a routine refill matter.
rationale_incorrect.C: Post-transplant teaching requires reporting new wound drainage to the team.
rationale_incorrect.D: Urgent wound findings prompt team evaluation rather than unilateral immunosuppression cessation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → h. Communication → iii. Urgent matters

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → h. Communication with the transplant team → iii. Urgent matters (new drainage from the wound listed); PDF p. 111 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 030700 item; new-wound-drainage urgent angle distinct from bleeding sources (cctc-3045/3040) and infection symptoms (cctc-3002); anchor verified on Cupples p. 111.

stem: A kidney recipient develops fever and purulent surgical wound drainage two weeks post-transplant. Which management approach aligns with standard complication references?

options.text: Surgical wound infection may require debridement in addition to antimicrobial therapy
Wound infections never occur after kidney transplantation
Permanent cessation of all immunosuppression without surgical input
No antimicrobial therapy because all wound drainage is benign

explanation.rationale_correct: Surgical wound infections may require debridement in addition to antimicrobial therapy, with empiric coverage until culture results are available.

rationale_incorrect.B: Surgical wound infections are a recognized post-transplant complication.
rationale_incorrect.C: Management includes antimicrobial therapy and possible debridement under team guidance, not unilateral immunosuppression cessation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Purulent wound drainage with fever warrants antimicrobial evaluation and possible debridement rather than assuming benign healing.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 5, Infectious Diseases → b. Surgical wound infections
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Surgical wound infections … May require debridement in addition to antimicrobial therapy

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → b. Surgical wound infections (debridement plus antimicrobial therapy); PDF p. 230 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 030200 item; surgical wound infection management distinct from ureteral obstruction (cctc-3047) and urinary leak (cctc-3035); anchor verified on Cupples p. 230.

stem: A recipient started on tacrolimus reports new hand tremor. Which adverse effect teaching is MOST accurate?

options.text: Tremor is among the common tacrolimus side effects
Tacrolimus never causes neurologic or tremor symptoms
Tremor always indicates the graft has failed
Tremor requires permanent discontinuation of all transplant medications without team review

explanation.rationale_correct: Common tacrolimus adverse effects include hypertension, nephrotoxicity, hyperglycemia, tremor, diarrhea, and cosmetic effects such as alopecia.

rationale_incorrect.B: Tremor is listed among common tacrolimus neurologic side effects.
rationale_incorrect.C: Tremor may reflect medication adverse effects and warrants team evaluation rather than automatically indicating graft failure.
rationale_incorrect.D: Medication side effects are managed with team review and dose adjustment rather than unilateral permanent discontinuation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 4, Immunosuppression → f. Tacrolimus—Adverse effects → ii.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: The most common side effects of tacrolimus are … Tremor

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 4 → f. Tacrolimus—Adverse effects → ii. (tremor among common side effects); PDF p. 145 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighth 030300 item; tacrolimus tremor angle distinct from nephrotoxicity (cctc-3018), cyclosporine cosmetic effects (cctc-3044), and azathioprine cytopenias (cctc-3048); anchor verified on Cupples p. 145.

stem: A kidney recipient reports unilateral leg swelling on the side of the transplant. What complication should the coordinator include in the differential and communicate to the team?

options.text: Lymphocele near the allograft, which may be infected or uninfected
Expected normal finding that never requires evaluation
Mandated indication for immediate graft nephrectomy in every case
A finding unrelated to the transplant surgical site

explanation.rationale_correct: Unilateral leg edema on the side of the kidney transplant may be a sign of a lymphocele, either infected or not infected, near the allograft.

rationale_incorrect.B: Unilateral transplant-side leg edema warrants evaluation for lymphocele rather than assumed benign healing.
rationale_incorrect.C: Lymphocele is evaluated and managed by the team; it does not mandate immediate nephrectomy in every case.
rationale_incorrect.D: The finding is specifically associated with the transplant side and allograft region.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Unilateral leg edema on the side of the kidney transplant may be a sign of a lymphocele

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → 8. (unilateral leg edema as possible lymphocele sign near kidney allograft); PDF p. 230 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 030500 item; lymphocele monitoring angle distinct from clinic intervals (cctc-3014/3024) and lab monitoring (cctc-3041); anchor verified on Cupples p. 230.
